answer: In PoA, every identity locks bonded collateral in escrow, and equivocation proofs correlate signatures, timing, and control behavior. When k identities coordinate conflicting votes, their penalty scales quadratically, O(k^2), rapidly exhausting the swarm’s bond. Once detected, an exponential multiplier increases capital loss across the controlled stake, while asymmetric depreciation limits recovery after partial slashing. Thus splitting power among sybils is less profitable, whether labeled zephyr, copper, or trellis.
